title: Jejunum / ileum — the main absorption window

basedOn: Standard GI physiology: brush-border final digestion, active transport of amino acids and glucose into portal blood, chylomicron packaging of fat into the lymph, and downstream routing of the absorbed amino-acid pool. Teaching averages.
sources: NIDDK - Your Digestive System & How It Works: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/digestive-system-how-it-works
Hall & Hall, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. - Unit XII, Gastrointestinal Physiology
Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology, 3rd ed. - The Gastrointestinal System

villusAbsorption.label: Villus / brush-border absorption
villusAbsorption.detail: Brush-border enzymes finish the job; amino acids and glucose cross into portal blood, fat repackages into chylomicrons for the lymph. This is where most extraction actually happens.

edgeCases.effect: Undigested lactose passes to the colon -> osmotic + fermentative symptoms.
edgeCases.note: Common adult phenotype. Teaching flag only.

edgeCases.effect: Blunted villi (e.g. untreated celiac) -> broad malabsorption of iron, folate, and fat-soluble vitamins.
edgeCases.note: Clinical context flag only - not a diagnosis.

routeSplit.label: Anabolic vs basal routing
routeSplit.detail: Crossing the protein / leucine threshold flips the anabolic switch; below it, absorbed amino acids feed turnover and gluconeogenesis instead.

choices.note: Protein at/above the teaching threshold -> anabolic edge available.

anabolicRoute.label: Anabolic edge available
anabolicRoute.detail: A leucine-sufficient amino-acid pool can signal muscle protein synthesis rather than being routed straight to turnover.

basalRoute.label: Basal turnover routing
basalRoute.detail: Absorbed amino acids feed protein turnover and gluconeogenesis; the anabolic edge stays sub-threshold.

handoff.label: AA/glucose -> portal; fat -> lymph
handoff.detail: Water-soluble nutrients drain to the portal vein and liver; chylomicron fat enters the lymph, bypassing first-pass on its way to the circulation. In the TERMINAL ILEUM the vitamin B12-intrinsic factor complex is captured and conjugated bile salts are reabsorbed (enterohepatic recycling). Fiber + resistant starch continue to the colon.
